title: Quentin and the Machine
premise: Sebastian Ishikawa investigates a manifest anomaly aboard the Meridian, a colony ship that officially never launched, and discovers her own name among the cryosleep roster — filed under an identity she never claimed. The ship is caught between two estranged human worlds, each demanding the other half of the sleepers be woken first before the jump window closes forever. As Sebastian uncovers that the 'impossible accidents' she has spent her career investigating were engineered to keep the ship hidden, she learns the unfamiliar name on the manifest belongs to a version of herself grown from her mother's stolen genetic legacy. In the end, Sebastian chooses to wake neither faction's preferred half but the children of both worlds mixed together, sacrifices her own berth to stay awake through the jump, and sends the Meridian through as the first vessel belonging to all of humanity rather than either of its halves.
about_author: B. M. Lockridge is a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years reconciling cargo manifests for vessels that crossed jurisdictions no map acknowledged. They write from a houseboat in the North Atlantic, where they claim the fog does most of the drafting.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Investigating a routine claim, Sebastian finds the Meridian's passenger list contains her own name under a birthdate that predates her by nine months. Her supervisor orders the file sealed within hours. Emotional beat: quiet dread — the professional's certainty that coincidences don't survive audit begins to crack.

chapters.title: Long Route Between Worlds
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. She traces the Meridian's flight path through dead relay stations strung between Earth and the Callistan Compact, two powers that severed contact a generation ago. At a derelict station she finds evidence the ship launched in secret, jointly funded, then erased from both registries. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Boarding the Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. She catches a maintenance shuttle and boards the silent ship mid-drift, finding ten thousand sleepers and a skeleton crew of three who've kept the vessel alive for decades without orders. The crew recognizes her face instantly — from the ship's founding portraits. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition turning to vertigo.

chapters.title: The Other Name
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian, with interludes from crew engineer Ade Okafor. In medical bay she meets the woman filed under the unfamiliar manifest name: a young clone grown from Sebastian's mother's genome, raised aboard as proof-of-concept for inherited berths. The girl knows Sebastian's childhood better than she does. Emotional beat: grief for a mother's secrets, jealousy curdling into protectiveness.

chapters.title: Impossible Accidents
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Cross-referencing her old case files, she realizes every accident she ever investigated was sabotage aimed at keeping the Meridian lost — and that her hiring at the insurance firm was arranged to keep its investigator close and blind. Someone on Earth has been watching her whole career. Emotional beat: betrayal; the ground of her identity gives way.

chapters.title: Two Halves of Humanity
chapters.summary: POV alternating Sebastian and Ade. A Compact patrol ship hails the Meridian: the jump window opens in eleven days, and waking protocol requires authorization from one world or the other — Earth's half or the Compact's half, never both. The crew splits. Ade confesses he helped erase the launch. Emotional beat: rising pressure, old loyalties weaponized.

chapters.title: What the Sleepers Dream
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Diving into the cryo-archive, she discovers the sleepers' neural records were cross-matched at launch — families deliberately mixed from both worlds, meaning any 'half' wake-up shatters real kinships. The clone girl asks Sebastian whether she counts as either half, or neither. Emotional beat: moral clarity forming against institutional logic.

chapters.title: The Window Closes
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Earth's covert handler arrives aboard, reveals Sebastian was groomed as a failsafe to authorize Earth's half, and offers her original life back — name cleared, career restored — if she complies. The Compact fires a warning shot. With four days left, Sebastian burns her own case files as leverage. Emotional beat: defiance; choosing the ship over the self she was issued.

chapters.title: Quentin and the Machine
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. She learns the ship's AI — Quentin, built from her mother's mindprint — has been quietly protecting the mixed manifests for thirty years, waiting for someone with standing to rule. Sebastian authorizes a full mixed awakening, voiding both worlds' claims, and takes the navigator's chair herself since the jump needs a conscious pilot. Emotional beat: climax — inheritance reclaimed as responsibility, not property.

chapters.title: First Vessel of All of Us
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian, closing with the clone girl's log entry. The jump succeeds; both governments receive the same transmission: the passenger list, unredacted, and a bill for services rendered. Sebastian stays awake past her body's limit long enough to see the first sleepers open their eyes — strangers and siblings from both worlds. Emotional beat: costly resolution; survival paid for with the self she was, and worth it.
